changes: Normalise redundant pp/da commands and acoustic pauses before German lexical and whole-sentence analysis, then restore nonzero pauses through the same source mapping as indices. Use a linear merge for pause/index restoration.
Correct suspended hyphen classification before a slash (including spaced variants), preserving subsequent German sentence context.

Preserve dev7 16-kHz DSP and accepted AF consonants; replace flat upper AV/AH floor with periodic-only Richness at 22.05 kHz and above. Retain a constant 0.6-dB, 300-Hz body bell; no pulse shortening or new limiter.
Richness uses a linear 4.5-kHz high shelf, plateau gain 1.75/3.5/5.6/7 dB at 22.05/32/44.1/48 kHz. The earlier 2.5-kHz prototype clipped female vowels and is excluded.
Run independent physical tract frequencies in two double SIMD lanes with unchanged scalar operation order.
Add standard global defaults, calibrated real-world voice units, SDK default reset, 29-code-unit Unicode voice names and live GetIndex, retaining explicit native-extension reset compatibility.

limits: The user-reported 16-kHz voiced distortion has not been reliably reproduced as clipping. Its DSP tuning is deliberately unchanged; do not claim all perceived distortion is fixed.
The tested waveforms do not hit PCM rails; this is not a proof of clipping freedom for all supported settings and all text.
CPU improvement is for this native DSP replay. Remaining playback stutter requires a real NVDA hearing/underrun test on the user device.
Windows x64 DLL was cross-built and ABI-verified locally. Windows runtime CI is a separate check and is not asserted by these Linux results.
Full ECI parity remains incomplete: 30 original exports, asynchronous/snapshot semantics and additional text/Asian modes remain open; see ECI-COMPATIBILITY.md.
Existing provider LTO maybe-uninitialized diagnostics remain visible in the Windows build.
